title: Archipelago IO - Path to First Call, Credits & Deployment Options
summary: Introductory discovery focused on quickstart/free credits, expected time-to-first-token, and initial deployment fit. Customer is early-stage platform team evaluating Hosted API for rapid prototyping with a potential move to Dedicated or Private (VPC) for production. Key concerns: latency SLA, cost per token, SSO/KMS, and auditability. Next step is a short pilot using free credits and a benchmark window; Redwood to send pricing, SOC2 docs, and an SE-run latency test plan.
topics: Latency vs cost tradeoffs and sample benchmarks
next_steps: Maya to send pricing + pilot scope deck by 2026-05-28
Ethan to share latency test template and benchmark checklist by 2026-06-01
Archipelago to provide sample prompt set and expected QPS by 2026-05-29
action_items: Maya Singh: Send pricing sheet, pilot scope, link to quickstart docs (due 2026-05-28)
Ethan Park: Create and send latency/throughput test plan + sample benchmark script (due 2026-06-01)
Nora Patel: Share sample prompt set, PII / reg constraints, and traffic profile (due 2026-05-29)
Olivia Gomez: Confirm VPC requirements and whitelist IP ranges for pilot (due 2026-05-30)
transcript:
00:00 Maya Singh: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, AE on the account. Quick roll call?
00:08 Nora Patel: Nora here, CTO at Archipelago. Samir, Olivia, Ravi on too.
00:12 Samir Reddy: Hey all, Samir. Lead ML.
00:15 Olivia Gomez: Olivia, infra.
: 00:18 Maya Singh: Nice. Ethan, want to intro yourself?
00:20 Ethan Park: Yeah hi, Ethan Park, SE. I work on performance and private deployment flows.
00:25 Maya Singh: Great. We're aiming for 45 minutes — cover quickstart credits, time to first token, and how folks typically choose between Hosted, Dedicated, and Private. Then figure out pilot next steps. Sound good?
00:33 Nora Patel: Yep, that's exactly it. We're trying to prototype a generative API feature for our product search and want to understand cost and latency tradeoffs.
00:40 Maya Singh: Perfect. Samir — can you give a quick picture of current infra and what you're trying to build?
00:45 Samir Reddy: Sure. Right now search is microservices in k8s on GCP. We have a small ML infra team — model training happens elsewhere, inference we want to centralize. Prototype needs to hit 90th percentile latencies under 250ms for short prompts, QPS ~10-20 for the first month. Long term we expect bursts to 200 QPS. Data privacy: some user queries have PII; we need audit logs and enterprise retention controls.
01:10 Maya Singh: Good context. So typical path we see: teams do a quickstart on Redwood Hosted API using free credits to validate model behavior and accuracy, then evaluate Dedicated capacity if they need sustained throughput and predictable latency, or Private (VPC/on-prem) if they have strict network or compliance needs.
01:26 Nora Patel: Makes sense. Two questions: how fast can we get a test call running, and what's in the free credits?
01:32 Maya Singh: You can have a token and a first call in under an hour if you follow the quickstart. Free credits are flexible — usually a small pool to run evaluation queries; I'll include the exact voucher details in the follow-up.
01:42 Ethan Park: For latency, a quick note: hosted instances vary by model and sequence length. For short prompts and smaller models you can see sub-100ms p95 in our benchmarks, but that depends on model, quantization, and routing. We can run a brief benchmark with your prompt set to get realistic numbers.
01:58 Samir Reddy: That would be helpful. We care about p95 more than average. Also do you support KV cache and streaming? Our UX uses streaming to show tokens live.
02:08 Ethan Park: Yes on streaming; KV cache support exists for models with context caching, and we have prefix/cache strategies to reduce cost for repeated prompts.
02:15 Olivia Gomez: On the security side: SOC2, SSO (SAML/Okta), KMS for keys — do you support customer-managed keys?
02:23 Maya Singh: Short answer yes to SOC2 and SSO. For KMS, customer-managed keys are supported on Private deployments and we have integrations with cloud KMS for Dedicated in many enterprise contracts. Hosted can integrate with managed KMS in the future; I'll confirm specifics in the follow up.
02:40 Nora Patel: And audit logs — can we get token-level logs for requests and responses? We need to show lineage for compliance.
02:47 Ethan Park: We surface request metadata, timestamps, latencies — for full request/response capture we have options but we push practice to mask or redact PII. On Dedicated and Private you can configure retention and raw logs export to your SIEM.
02:59 Maya Singh: Let's talk pilots: we typically do a 2-week pilot using the quickstart credits. SE runs a short benchmark with your prompts, we evaluate accuracy/regression, and measure latency/cost. If you want predictable SLOs, Dedicated is the next step. Private is for VPC or air-gapped use.
03:16 Ravi Menon: Timeline wise, we want an internal demo in three weeks and a decision on pilot by mid-June.
03:22 Maya Singh: That's doable. We'll aim to have the pilot scope and pricing to you in 48 hours.
03:26 Nora Patel: Cool. On cost: can you give a rough range for token pricing and Dedicated minimums?
03:31 Maya Singh: I'll send exact tiers, but high level: hosted pay-as-you-go per token, embeddings separate. Dedicated has a monthly reserved capacity with a baseline commit; costs depend on model family and quantization. We can model your expected monthly token consumption for better numbers.
03:45 Samir Reddy: Is there an easy way to simulate token consumption? We have long conversations that might hit few thousand tokens per session for power users.
03:51 Ethan Park: We have a cost estimator template — we'll tailor it to your prompt set. For long sessions, batching and KV caching reduce effective per-token cost. Also quantized variants of models can be cheaper with modest quality tradeoffs.
04:06 Maya Singh: Any constraints with on-prem? Olivia?
04:09 Olivia Gomez: On-prem would be last resort — compliance heavy option. For now VPC peering or private deployment through our VPC would be the ask. We need to know IP ranges, egress, and whether we can route through our firewall.
04:20 Ethan Park: We do VPC connectivity for Private with customer managed control plane. For Dedicated we can do private peering options. We'll include network runbook and expected IP ranges in the follow-up.
04:30 Nora Patel: Great. One other question — data retention and model training. Do you retrain on customer data? Are prompts used to fine tune upstream models?
04:37 Maya Singh: By default hosted models do not use customer prompts to retrain. We offer opt-in options and private deployments keep data customer-controlled. We'll include the data handling policy in the docs we send.
04:48 Samir Reddy: Okay. For the pilot, we want to target the p95 threshold under 250ms for short prompts. Can you outline what the benchmark will look like?
04:57 Ethan Park: Sure — SE-run plan: 1) baseline cold start latency, 2) steady-state p50/p95 at target QPS, 3) throughput until latency degradation. We'll run both hosted and a Dedicated-config sim if needed, use your prompt set to ensure realistic token lengths. I'll send the script and a short python client you can run.
05:17 Nora Patel: Sounds solid. We'll need to ensure the pilot doesn't expose raw responses with PII. Can we redact in-flight?
05:23 Ethan Park: We can enable redaction and configurable masking on logs. For the pilot we'll configure minimal logs and anonymize payloads.
05:31 Maya Singh: Quick qualification — who on Archipelago will own the pilot internally?
05:34 Nora Patel: Samir will own ML side, Olivia infra, and Ravi will coordinate product.
05:39 Maya Singh: Perfect. Any competitors you're seeing?
05:41 Ravi Menon: We've looked at OpenAI and Anthropic for quick experiments; GCP Vertex for integrated infra. Two main things that are tripping us up: predictability of latency and the ability to go private later.
05:53 Maya Singh: That's a common thread. For predictability Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and SLA; Private gives you full control but higher ops. Hosted is best for speed to prototype.
06:05 Nora Patel: Are there customers similar to us who've done hosted-to-dedicated migration?
06:08 Ethan Park: Yes, a couple of mid-market SaaS companies. We can share a short case study and a migration checklist showing how they pinned model versions and rolled out canaries.
06:18 Maya Singh: I'll include that. For immediate next steps: I'll send pricing, credits voucher, SOC2 and data-handling policy, and a pilot scope doc. Ethan will send the benchmark.
06:28 Samir Reddy: On benchmarks, can you also include a rough cost projection for 50k tokens/day and 500k tokens/day?
06:34 Maya Singh: Yes, we'll do a short cost model with a low/medium/high usage scenario.
06:39 Olivia Gomez: Also, for SSO — we use Okta and SAML, we need RBAC for team members.
06:44 Ethan Park: RBAC is supported in Console for Dedicated and Private; hosted has scaled role constructs and SSO integrations. We'll detail the exact SAML metadata steps.
06:56 Nora Patel: Are there any operational gotchas when moving from hosted to private we should plan for?
07:01 Ethan Park: Ops-wise, network configuration and key management are biggest. You'll need either peering or a private link; if you want customer-managed KMS in Private we'll walk through HSM/KMS rotation policies. Also model compatibility — some custom quantized builds take minor tuning.
07:18 Samir Reddy: On model variants — do you surface performance profiles per model? We want to pick a family that balances latency and output quality.
07:25 Ethan Park: We maintain a model catalog with performance profiles and recommended quantization levels per architecture. For your prompts we can run a quality regression test alongside latency to make a tradeoff recommendation.
07:37 Maya Singh: Quick check — does Archipelago have any legal/procurement constraints? Contracts team, PO timelines?
07:42 Nora Patel: We have standard SaaS T&Cs, procurement lead will review for Dedicated/Private because of the commitment. We can share procurement timeline after the pilot.
07:50 Maya Singh: Good. We'll leave the contract talk until after pilot. Any final questions?
07:54 Ravi Menon: One small ask — can we get a sample integration snippet in Go? Our backend is go heavy.
07:59 Ethan Park: Yep, we have SDKs in several languages; I'll add a Go snippet to the quickstart pack.
08:06 Maya Singh: Okay recap: 1) Maya sends pricing, credits, SOC2, data policy, pilot scope (due 5/28). 2) Ethan sends latency/throughput test plan + sample python client + Go snippet (due 6/1). 3) Archipelago shares prompts and traffic profile (due 5/29). 4) Schedule pilot week of 6/2. Any objections?
08:27 Nora Patel: No objections.
08:29 Maya Singh: Great, we'll follow up. Thank you all.
08:32 Samir Reddy: Thanks.
08:33 Olivia Gomez: Thanks, bye.
08:34 End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional word swaps (e.g., "KV cache" heard as "kay vee cache"), minor timestamps approximate; speaker labels derived from calendar invite. Some domain terms may be slightly mistranscribed (quantization -> quanta zation).
